sections.h2: How Islip property tax collection works
sections.html:
Islip bills through its Receiver of Taxes, and the cycle runs from December to May. Collection opens December 1, bills go out around the second week of December, and the full year's tax is due on or before January 10. Owners who prefer to split the payment pay half by January 10 and the other half by May 31.

You get one bill a year. If your lender escrows the tax, the December bill goes to the lender, and you will receive a statement in February after the first half is paid and another in July after the second. A bill that never reaches you is not a defense, since state law keeps the owner responsible, and the town cannot waive a penalty.

The 2026-2027 tax year begins on December 1, 2026, and details are posted in early to mid December 2026. Taxes become a lien each December 1. Nobody can pay ahead of time, because the Receiver does not know the amount until the warrant arrives from the Suffolk County Legislature.

For a seller, the practical timeline looks like this. In early December the amount becomes known and the lien attaches. By January 10 you either pay everything or the first half. Between January and May each month adds a point to whatever is open. On May 31 the town's window closes. If you plan to list in winter or spring, find out in December which of those stages your bill is in, because the answer decides how much the buyer's title company will hold back at closing.

After January 10 the penalty goes up by one point at the start of each month and stops at 5% for payments made from May 11 to May 31. A partial payment is accepted in person or by mail at any point until May 31, with a minimum of $200 plus any penalty due.

Islip late penalty by payment date
When taxes are submittedPenalty added
From December 1 to January 10None
After January 101%
After February 102%
After March 103%
After April 104%
From May 11 to May 315%

Whatever is unpaid on June 1 leaves the town's hands. The Suffolk County Comptroller, 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, (631) 852-3000, takes over with additional penalty and interest.

sections.h2: Who sets an Islip assessment, and when is Grievance Day?
sections.html:
The Town Assessor's Office, at 40 Nassau Avenue, values more than 99,000 parcels and approves exemptions. Its phone is (631) 224-5585. Regular hours are 8:30 am to 4 pm, Monday through Friday. A property search on the town site shows the assessment for a particular parcel.

Islip follows the Suffolk pattern, so Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in May. For the next cycle that is May 18, 2027, and the tentative roll is finalized on or before May 1. Hand-deliver complaints to Suite 3 at 40 Nassau Avenue. A complaint that reaches the Assessor after 9 pm that day is dismissed as untimely. Board of Assessment Review decisions arrive by regular mail on or about July 1.

  • Informal review: before March 1, the Assessor will look at written proof of value, such as a refinance appraisal dated within a year of July 1 or a nearby arm's-length sale.
  • Assessment estimates: on written request, the office gives a one-year estimate before you add a pool, bathroom or addition.
  • Court review: if the board says no, New York's Small Claims Assessment Review costs $30 for an owner-occupied one to three family home and must start within 30 days of the final roll.

The town administers exemptions for senior citizens, persons with disabilities, volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers, home improvement, agricultural land, business, religious and not-for-profit owners, military service, and first-time buyers of a newly constructed home. Every application or renewal is due at the Assessor's Office by March 1.

The senior citizen and disability exemptions use a sliding scale for incomes up to $58,400. The Town Board raised that ceiling in October 2022 from the earlier $37,400. For the 2027/28 year, applications with 2025 income proof are due by March 1, 2027. Seniors apply at Suite 2 (631-224-5058) and persons with disabilities at Suite 3 (631-224-5585).

Basic STAR covers owner-occupied primary homes where the owners and spouses earn less than $250,000, and it removes the first $30,000 of full value from school tax. Enhanced STAR serves owners aged 65 and up with income under $113,550 for 2027/28, and the state will upgrade Basic to Enhanced automatically. For STAR help call the state at 518-457-2036.

sections.h2: What to know about Islip tax before selling
sections.html:
Because tax is a lien from December 1, a sale between December and May needs a payoff for the current year. Ask the Receiver where the bill stands, and then check the title company's search for earlier years.

  • A new owner's name can take up to six months after closing to show on the bill. The December bill follows ownership as of March 1.
  • If the bill shows the word RESTORATION, the prior owner had exemptions the buyer cannot keep, and the buyer repays them once, in that tax year.
  • Owners who finish paying a mortgage should call the Receiver so the records change.
  • The mailing address change form sits in the Forms section of the town site.

A cash buyer can take a house with an open tax balance and pay it from the closing proceeds, so penalties stop stacking while the sale is pending. If the house has a senior or disability exemption, tell the buyer early so the restoration amount is not a surprise. Before closing, line up three things: the Receiver's balance for the current year, the title search for older years, and a written note of any exemption the buyer will lose.

Islip is a South Shore town in Suffolk County covering 103.2 square miles of land. Villages are Brightwaters, Islandia, Ocean Beach and Saltaire, and hamlets include Bay Shore, Brentwood, Central Islip, Sayville, West Islip and Ronkonkoma. The town estimates 340,867 residents for July 2025 and 102,205 households. Owners occupy 80.5% of homes with a median value of $535,300, median rent is $2,209, and median household income is $130,132. The Long Island Rail Road serves the area, which helps listings near a station. Taxes here are billed once a year with a hard lien date, so buyers and title companies look at the status of the current bill first. A seller who can hand over a clear Receiver statement and a list of exemptions in place saves days during the contract period.

faqs.q: When does Islip property tax collection start?
faqs.a: Collection for 2026-2027 opens December 1, 2026. Bills are mailed around the second week of December, and the first half is due on or before January 10.

faqs.q: Can I pay Islip property tax early?
faqs.a: No. The Receiver does not know the amounts until the warrant comes from the Suffolk County Legislature in early December.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Islip tax after May 31?
faqs.a: To the Suffolk County Comptroller, 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901. The phone number is (631) 852-3000, and penalty and interest are added.

faqs.q: What is the Islip Grievance Day for 2027?
faqs.a: It is the third Tuesday in May, so May 18, 2027. A complaint must reach the Assessor's Office by 9 pm that day or the Board of Assessment Review dismisses it as untimely.

faqs.q: Why does my Islip bill show the previous owner?
faqs.a: The December bill is built from ownership as of March 1, and a closing after that date can take up to six months to show in the system. The new owner still owes the tax.
